title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'when do we satisfy?' hints dual satisfaction; only one from Christ
pass_a_gloss: 'When do we finally satisfy by his actual satisfaction?' nearly mocks itself. It smuggles a second, habitual satisfaction. There is no such twin: only Christ's one satisfaction in our stead—unlike Adam's actual act versus the habitual vice propagated into us.
pass_b_english: Next the question, When then at last do we satisfy in Christ by his actual satisfaction? is not far from ridiculous: for it hints a double satisfaction, actual and habitual; whereas yet not, as there is one actual sin committed by Adam, another habitual propagated into us and inhering in us, so is there any satisfaction besides that which was performed by Christ in our place.
source_text: Deinde quaestio, Quando vero demum satisfacimus in Christo satisfactione eius actuali? parum abest quin sit ridicula: innuit enim duplicem satisfactionem, actualem & habitualem; cum tamen non, ut est peccatum aliud actuale ab Adamo commissum, aliud habituale in nos propagatum ac nobis inhaerens, sic ulla sit satisfactio praeter eam quae a Christo loco nostro praestita est.
